correctness.rationale: Under the strict parameter bounds, conditioning on the two-sided environment gives independent patch noises and the recursion for the conditional mean; its variance yields C0. Cross-lag conditional means yield C1/C0=(lambda+rho)/(1+lambda rho), and residual same-patch persistence yields A1-C1=lambda[p(1-p)-C0]. Because C0 and E of the conditional variance are strictly positive and |q|<1, all four parameters are globally reconstructed. Distinct rational admissible models with one-date law (13/50,6/25,6/25,13/50) prove sharpness. A standalone exact 8-state rational stationary solver verified 12 parameter settings, 768 transition entries, 48 moments and 12 inversions; enumeration alone is not claimed as general proof.

value.rationale: Separating shared environmental Markov memory from local patch persistence is a motivated ecological synchrony problem. The theorem proves exact structural recoverability from one mean and three second moments using only two adjacent census dates and proves sharp failure for one date in the same two-patch setting. The exact sharp boundary is useful for designing and interpreting paired-occupancy observations, despite not guaranteeing finite-sample precision or stability under misspecification.
